newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita April-June group profit seen rising 50%.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita April-June group profit seen rising 50%.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd is expected to report a 50 percent year-on-year jump in its group operating profit for the April-June quarter, with a recovery in sales continuing in almost all of its products, analysts say.

The yen's weakening also should have dramatically improved business of export-dependent units such as Matsushita-Kotobuki Electronics Industries Ltd, which were hit hard by the strong yen a year ago, they said.
"It's hard to find unfavourable factors," said Hideki Watanabe, analyst at Nikko Research Centre.
"Sales are strong both in domestic and overseas markets thanks to the low yen."
Matsushita will announce group-based earnings for the first quarter of fiscal 1996/97 at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) on Tuesday.
Goldman Sachs (Japan) analyst Hitoshi Kuriyama said he expected a 52.5 percent gain year-on-year in the company's group operating profit for the first quarter.
Sales of information-related goods, such as cellular phones, may have gained 15 percent, while a 2.7 percent sales increase is expected in home appliances, he said.
Industry analysts expect strong housing starts to help push up domestic shipments of refrigerators, air conditioners, televisions and washing machines to record highs in calendar 1996.

Some other analysts said they were focusing on the level of Matsushita's product inventories in China, where despite having a big share of the market for audiovisual products it suffers from slow sales due to strict government regulations.
